text:
Emma (Product Designer): Quick sync 1: should the usage chart legend show tokens or dollars by default when a user lands on the org page? We have mixed feedback.

Raj (PM): Org-level folks mostly want dollars. Teams/users who are debugging care about tokens. Maybe context-aware default: org->dollars, project->tokens.

Lina (Frontend Eng): Technical note: we can render axis/value transforms client-side. Persisting user pref is the heavier piece (needs settings API).

Sam (Data Viz): Also think about time window. For short ranges tokens are more meaningful; for monthly aggregates dollars are cleaner. We can auto-switch based on selected range but must avoid surprise flips.

Maya (Accessibility): If auto-switching happens, announce it to screen readers (aria-live) and provide a clear manual toggle. The toggle should be reachable via keyboard and have an accessible name like "Display units: dollars or tokens".

Dave (Billing): From billing ops: the conversion to dollars must use the account's effective rate (committed discounts, credits). If we show an estimate we need a small "est." label and link to billing details. Also ensure CSV exports include both columns when users choose tokens.

Nora (Analytics): For telemetry, add events: unit_toggle, unit_auto_switch, and export_units_selected. We need product metrics to see adoption.

Emma: UX proposal: inline toggle on chart (top-right), default based on scope & time range, with a tiny inline conversion row: "500k tokens ≈ $42 (est.)" collapsed by default. Add a ? tooltip explaining when tokens are useful.

Raj (PM): Sounds good. UX question: should the export button respect the chart unit or always include dollars?

Dave (Billing): Exports should always include canonical billing amounts (dollars). Add an optional column for tokens if user selected tokens. Don't overwrite invoices.

Lina (Frontend Eng): Implementation checklist: toggle component, settings persistence endpoint, aria-live hook, conversion call to billing API, CSV exporter change. Estimate ~3 dev days + QA.

Sam (Data Viz): Chart behavior: when switching units, animate the value change (fade/slide) and keep x-axis ticks stable. Avoid re-scaling that jumps users' eyes.

Maya (Accessibility): Tooltip copy idea: "Tokens = raw model usage (helpful for perf and quota). Dollars = billed cost. Toggle to view either." Keep it short. Provide sr-only full sentence for the toggle state.

Emma: I'll add designs to Figma: frame id "usage-units-inline-toggle". Key states: default dollars (org monthly), tokens (project short window), conversion row expanded.

Raj (PM): Edge case: projects on committed plans with blended rates. Conversion must surface a little info icon: "Effective rate includes discounts". Link to billing page.

Dave (Billing): Agreed. Also we need to cache rates for performance and invalidate on billing changes. If rate missing, show tokens-only with a note "conversion unavailable".

Nora (Analytics): Add a dimension to the toggle telemetry for scope (org/project), time_window, and account_plan_type.

Lina (Frontend Eng): Small CSS nit: ensure the inline toggle doesn't wrap on small widths. Maybe collapse into an overflow menu on mobile.

Maya (Accessibility): On mobile, ensure the toggle is still keyboard and screen-reader accessible; use native <button> with aria-pressed states.

Emma: Action items I will own: add Figma variants + tooltip copy. Lina to own implementation ticket. Sam to provide animation guidance. Maya to review a11y checklist. Dave to provide billing API contract for rates. Nora will add analytics spec.

billing-bot: Billing rate API mock available at https://internal-api.redwood-inference/billing/v1/rates?account_id=xxx (mock/stub).

Lina (Frontend Eng): I'll pick this up after current sprint, seems like 4-5 story points. Will post an RFC for the settings API persistence.

Emma: Thanks team 60; will update Figma and ping again when mocks are ready.

Raj (PM): Nice! Let's keep the toggle minimal and don't overwhelm the chart UI. :thumbsup:

Dave (Billing): One last thought: for legal/customer-facing invoices we never change unit labels away from dollars. Keep that rule.

Sam (Data Viz): Agreed. Charts are exploratory; invoices are canonical.
